hook.en: An Indian engineer in Dubai sends her salary home; a Japanese company in Bengaluru sends its profit to Tokyo. Which of these belong to India's GDP, and which to India's national income?
hook.kn: ದುಬೈನಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರ್ ಸಂಬಳವನ್ನು ಮನೆಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತಾಳೆ; ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನ ಜಪಾನಿ ಕಂಪನಿ ಲಾಭವನ್ನು ಟೋಕಿಯೋಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇವುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವುದು ಭಾರತದ GDP ಗೆ, ಯಾವುದು ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಆದಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರುತ್ತದೆ?

say.en: An Indian engineer in Dubai sends her salary home; a Japanese company in Bengaluru sends its profit to Tokyo. Which of these belong to India's GDP, and which to India's national income? In this lesson: Distinguish domestic and national aggregates.
Distinguish gross and net, market price and factor cost.
Compute GNP, NNP and national income.

title.en: Domestic vs national; gross vs net

body.en: GDP measures production within the *domestic* territory. GNP adds net factor income from abroad (NFIA): factor income earned by our residents abroad minus factor income earned by foreigners in our country. 'Gross' includes depreciation; 'net' subtracts it. So NNP = GNP − depreciation.
body.kn: GDP ದೇಶೀಯ ಭೂಪ್ರದೇಶದೊಳಗಿನ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ. GNP = GDP + ವಿದೇಶಗಳಿಂದ ನಿವ್ವಳ ಉತ್ಪಾದನಾಂಗ ಆದಾಯ (NFIA). 'ಒಟ್ಟು' ಎಂದರೆ ಸವಕಳಿ ಸೇರಿ; 'ನಿವ್ವಳ' ಎಂದರೆ ಸವಕಳಿ ಕಳೆದು. NNP = GNP − ಸವಕಳಿ.

GNP adds net factor income from abroad NFIA: factor income earned by our residents abroad minus factor income earned by foreigners in our country. 'Gross' includes depreciation; 'net' subtracts it. title.en: On the board: From GDP to national income

say.en: Start with GDP at market price: 2,000 crore.
Add net factor income from abroad, minus 20, to get GNP: 1,980.
Subtract depreciation of 150 to get NNP at market price: 1,830.
Subtract net indirect taxes, 180 minus 30, to get national income: 1,680.
Domestic to national: add NFIA. Gross to net: subtract depreciation. Market price to factor cost: subtract NIT.

caption.en: Start with GDP at market prices. Add net factor income from abroad to get GNP; subtract depreciation to get NNP; subtract net indirect taxes (indirect taxes − subsidies) to get NNP at factor cost, which is national income.

body.en: *Market prices* include indirect taxes and are lowered by subsidies. To find what the factors of production actually earn, we subtract net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies). NNP at factor cost is called national income. Personal income and personal disposable income are found from national income by further adjustments for undistributed profits, corporate tax, transfers and personal taxes.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. GDP at market price = ₹2,000 crore; NFIA = −₹20 crore; depreciation = ₹150 crore; indirect taxes = ₹180 crore; subsidies = ₹30 crore. Find GNP_MP, NNP_MP and national income.

say.en: Let us work through this together. GDP at market price equals 2,000 rupees crore; NFIA equals minus 20 rupees crore; depreciation equals 150 rupees crore; indirect taxes equals 180 rupees crore; subsidies equals 30 rupees crore. Find GNP MP, NNP MP and national income.
GNP MP equals 2000 plus minus 20 equals 1,980 rupees crore.
NNP MP equals 1980 minus 150 equals 1,830 rupees crore.
NIT equals 180 minus 30 equals 150 rupees crore.
National income equals NNP FC equals 1830 minus 150 equals 1,680 rupees crore.
So the answer is GNP MP 1,980 rupees cr; NNP MP 1,830 rupees cr; national income 1,680 rupees cr.
